SandCASTLE: A Portable, Economical, Environmentally Friendly
Habitat Printer for Low-Resource Communities

Description: One of the biggest problems faced by humans is a worldwide lack of affordable housing. Alternative technologies for building houses exist, namely 3D printing houses using cement, but this technology also has its downsides: since the 3D printer has to extrude 100% of the house material, the gantry must be large and strong, making these machines quite expensive, and the main ingredient in the cement, Portland cement, has a significant environmental footprint and must be transported to the building site. In this project, I designed, built, and demonstrated a novel 3D printer that uses a simple and low-cost motor and chain system to move the extruder head. In addition, I created a novel method of construction that takes advantage of the on-site sand material, where layers of this sand are laid out, smoothed out with the extruder head, and resin is selectively dispensed, also with the extruder head. A new layer of sand is poured on top, and this process is repeated until a fully 3D object has been created. As a proof-of-concept, I used my prototype printer to fabricate several test structures, including a small house structure. Compared to existing house 3D printers the equipment is a tiny fraction of the cost and size, a much tinier fraction of the final house’s mass needs to be transported to the site and extruded, and the materials themselves are much more environmentally friendly. This project received several awards, including placing 5th in the Applied Mechanics category at the 2026 California Science and Engineering Fair. I am continuing this project into the 26-27 school year, where I have several ideas on how to improve my design.

For an 8th grade project, I started BrickMoose, a company where I make unique LEGO sets detailing locations and sell them online. Over time, I continued to expand the number of sets, adding in local landmarks. I have also made partnerships with several physical stores. In early 2025 I [partnered with Destination PSP](https://destinationpsp.com/collections/brick-sets-inspired-by-palm-springs) to make a LEGO rendition of the iconic midcentury house design. This was so popular that we have since created 4 more unique sets for them, and they have overall purchased over 2000 units. As of August 2026, I have made 40+ different designs, over 5000 sets have been sold, and in-person sales are taking place in 10+ stores, including the MIT Museum and Destination PSP.

Description: I worked with Dr. Samantha Ying, Associate Professor of Soil Biogeochemistry at UCR, to create the internal electronics for the Ottersampler, a low-cost water sampler that can accurately monitor water quality over time to detect hazardous chemicals. To do this I went through multiple stages of PCB design, with the current iteration utilizing an ATMega328PB. It is currently being deployed to over 100 homes throughout California. I am actively continuing to work on this project by adding new features like water conductivity testing, while also consolidating components onto the PCB to simplify the Ottersampler’s assembly process.

I worked with with the Old Riverside Foundation, a local non-profit civic organization in Riverside, to create a detailed 3D model of the Weber house, a historic structure dating back to the 1930s. Currently utilizing photogrammetry software, Blender, and 3D printing to create a highly detailed 3D model of the house, along with improvements that had been planned.
